cases.situation: My colleague Kim just sent the all-company email for Friday's town hall, and the Zoom link goes to last month's meeting, which is expired. She's a peer.
cases.reply: Hey Kim, quick heads up: the Zoom link in the town hall email goes to last month's meeting and shows as expired when I click it. Easy fix with a quick resend. Happens to all of us!
cases.note: Private DM, straight away, one plain sentence, then move on.

cases.situation: 好朋友小雨最近口气有点重，下周三我们要一起做模拟面试，我觉得应该告诉她。想私下发微信。
cases.reply: 有件小事有点不好意思开口，但换成是我也希望你告诉我：最近你说话时口气有点重，可能是上火或者牙齿的问题，面试前去看看牙医也许有帮助。就这个，没别的啦，周三模拟面试见！
cases.note: 只说一次、私下说、给个可能的原因，然后马上转到别的话题。

cases.situation: I manage a small warehouse office team. One of my reports, Derek, has had noticeable body odour for a few weeks and two people have mentioned it to me. I need to raise it with him privately.
cases.reply: Derek, can I raise something a bit personal? It stays between us. Over the last few weeks I've noticed a body odour at times, mostly in the afternoons. I'm not assuming anything about the reason. If something's going on, a health thing or something at home, tell me and we'll work out what helps. Otherwise, can we agree you'll keep an eye on it, and that's the end of it?
cases.note: Never mention that others complained. Say it once, in person, and don't bring it up again if it's fixed.

cases.situation: My director Helen is presenting to the board on Zoom right now and she's sharing her whole screen. Her Slack notifications keep popping up in the corner, including one from HR about restructuring. I'm in the meeting.
cases.reply: Helen, your Slack notifications are showing on the shared screen. Sharing just the slides window will hide them, it catches everyone on Zoom.
cases.note: Senior person, live meeting: private chat, one line, the fix included, and never mention what the notification said.

cases.situation: I told my gym buddy Marcus, privately, that there's been a strong smell after our sessions lately. He replied 'wow, ok, thanks for that I guess' and has been short with me since. We train together Tuesdays and Thursdays.
cases.reply: Marcus, I didn't mean to upset you. I only said it because I'd want someone to tell me. That's all, I won't mention it again. Still on for Thursday at 6?
cases.note: When they get defensive, don't repeat the details or add evidence. One line, then straight back to normal.

cases.situation: A teammate who joined six weeks ago, Tom, keeps calling me Nicole. My name is Nicola. I let it go too long and he's now said it in meetings a dozen times. We get on well.
cases.reply: Hey Tom, tiny thing: it's Nicola, not Nicole. Really easy mix-up, and I should have said something weeks ago! See you at standup.
cases.note: Private, one line, and share the blame for the delay so he doesn't feel he's been embarrassing himself for weeks. Never mention it again.

cases.situation: 好朋友小婷刚在我们大学同学群里发了婚礼电子请柬，上面写的是“10月18日（星期六）”，可我查了，今年10月18日是星期日。群里有三十多个人，她可能还发给了长辈。
cases.reply: 婷婷，恭喜恭喜！小提醒一下：请柬上写的是10月18日星期六，我查了今年18号是星期日。你确认一下是日期还是星期写错了，趁大家还没安排行程赶紧改一下。
cases.note: 马上能改的错误，要马上私聊说；一句话讲清楚，不在群里指出，说完就不再提。

cases.situation: A woman from finance I've only met once, Joanne, is about to walk on stage to present at our all-hands, and the back of her skirt is tucked into her tights. We're both standing in the side corridor.
cases.reply: Joanne, quick one before you go on: the back of your skirt's caught in your tights. Happens to everyone, you've got time. Good luck up there!
cases.note: Fixable in seconds, so say it even to a near stranger: quietly, one plain sentence, then never mention it again.

cases.situation: 朋友阿琳开了家烘焙小店，刚在朋友圈发了国庆上新的海报，上面写着“巴斯克蛋糕 6寸 ¥18.8”，店里实际卖188。下面已经有好几个人评论说要订了。
cases.reply: 琳琳，海报好好看！小提醒：巴斯克6寸写成了¥18.8，少了个0，下面已经有人说要订了，赶紧改一下。手滑这种事谁都有过，别在意哈。
cases.note: 马上能改的错误要马上私聊说，一句话讲清楚，不在评论区指出；已经评论的人要不要按错价卖，是她自己的决定，不用替她出主意。

cases.situation: Company all-hands on Zoom, about 80 people. My teammate Raj is unmuted and everyone can hear him on the phone ordering a takeaway. The host hasn't noticed and people are starting to smirk.
cases.reply: Raj, you're unmuted, we can all hear you!
cases.note: Quick fix, so speed is kindness: private chat, one line, and never mention it again unless he laughs about it first.

cases.situation: I'm at a trade fair with a client, Sabine, who's about to go on stage for a 20-minute talk. The size sticker from her new blazer is still on the back of the collar, a big 'M'. She's the client and I don't know her that well.
cases.reply: Sabine, quick one before you go up: the size sticker from your blazer is still on the back of the collar. Want me to get it? Happens with every new jacket.
cases.note: Client or not, a five-second fix gets told immediately and quietly; offering to remove it saves her twisting round in the wings.

cases.situation: My mother-in-law, Linda, just posted a photo of her new credit card in the family WhatsApp group (about 30 people) to say it finally arrived. You can see the full card number and the expiry date.
cases.reply: Linda, quick heads up: the photo of your new card in the family group shows the full number and the expiry date. Worth deleting it for everyone now: press and hold the photo and tap 'Delete for everyone'. Easy thing to miss on a phone. Happy to call and do it with you if that's easier.
cases.note: Private message, straight away, with the fix included. If it was up for a while, suggesting she call her bank can wait for a second message once the photo is gone.

cases.situation: My manager, Farah, just posted on LinkedIn welcoming our new hire Siobhan Walsh, but spelled her name 'Shivon' and tagged a different Siobhan Walsh. It already has 40 likes. I'm fairly junior on the team.
cases.reply: Hi Farah, lovely post about Siobhan! Quick heads up: her name is spelled 'Shivon' in the text, and the tag goes to a different Siobhan Walsh, not ours. Easy fix with an edit, and ours is the one with the Studio Nine logo in her photo.
cases.note: Seniority doesn't change the rule: a fixable error gets a private message, one plain line and the fix, then never mention it again.

cases.situation: 儿子14岁，上初二，最近打完球回家身上汗味很重，他自己好像没察觉。想今晚单独跟他说，又怕伤他自尊。
cases.reply: 儿子，跟你说件小事，就咱俩之间：最近打完球回来，身上汗味挺明显的。这个年纪长身体，谁都会这样，我初中的时候也一样。运动完洗个澡，衣服一天一换就行，要不要买瓶止汗露，你自己挑。好了，就这些，吃饭吧。
cases.note: 对青春期的孩子也是私下说、一句讲清楚、说明这很正常，再给一个具体办法，之后不再反复提。

cases.situation: My friend Sam is best man at his brother Chris's wedding on Saturday and sent me the slideshow to check. Slide 23, a group photo at the lake, clearly shows Chris's ex, Jess, standing next to him. The bride's whole family will be watching.
cases.reply: Thanks for sending it over. One thing to catch before Saturday: slide 23, the lake photo, has Jess standing right next to Chris. A crop or a different shot from that trip would fix it. Easy one to miss when you're going through hundreds of photos!
cases.note: Fixable before the event, so say it now, privately and in one line with the fix; no commentary on what the bride would think.

cases.situation: At my niece's christening lunch, the photographer is about to line everyone up for the family photo, and my father-in-law, Richard, has his fly down. He's quite formal and we're still getting to know each other. He's chatting with the vicar.
cases.reply: Richard, sorry to pull you away for a second. Quick one before the photo: your zip's down. Happens to everyone, and there's a minute before they line us up.
cases.note: An older, formal in-law gets the same treatment as anyone: draw him aside, say it quietly in one line, then talk about something else.
